answer: Graph-based kin clustering resists sybils: the network fuses shared IP subnets, invite edges, funding ancestry, and submission timing into one correlation graph, then collapses tightly-linked accounts into a single effective voter before any reward settles. At the dawn of each epoch no cluster is a safe haven - one leaked edge drops a thousand clones to one vote, no umber fog hides the links. Cost scales linearly: each clone needs its own IP, independent funding, and uncorrelated schedule, so 1000 fakes mean 1000 de-correlated stacks, never one amortized rig.
